title: Chat / messaging app (WhatsApp, iMessage style)
summary: 1:1 and group chat with real-time delivery, offline send, read receipts, media, and push when backgrounded. The core is a local message store plus ordered, idempotent sync.
requirements: Send and receive text and media; delivery states (sending, sent, delivered, read); typing indicators.
Works offline: compose and queue; history available offline.
Real-time while foregrounded; notifications while backgrounded; multi-device.
components: Local DB: conversations, messages (indexed by conversation + sequence), outbox
Connection manager: WebSocket with heartbeat, reconnect with backoff, auth
Sync service: on connect/foreground, fetch messages after last sequence per conversation (REST)
Media service: upload to object storage via pre-signed URL first, then send message referencing it
Push: APNs alerts; Notification Service Extension to decrypt and show content
Crypto (if E2EE): identity keys in Keychain/Secure Enclave, Signal-style sessions
tradeoffs: Server-assigned per-conversation sequence numbers give total order and simple gap detection; client timestamps are unreliable.
WebSocket gives low latency but must be backed by REST sync for correctness after disconnects.
E2EE prevents server-side search and moderation and complicates multi-device (per-device keys, fan-out encryption).
Storing full history locally gives offline access and search but grows storage; offer media auto-download settings and cleanup.
body: **Send flow:** create message with client UUID, status `.sending`, insert into DB and outbox; UI shows it instantly. Send over socket (or REST fallback) with the client UUID as idempotency key. Server acks with sequence number and timestamp; client updates status to `.sent` and reorders if needed.
**Receive flow:** socket event or push → insert by (conversation, sequence) ignoring duplicates → if sequence gap detected, fetch missing range → send delivery receipt.
**Read receipts:** send the highest read sequence per conversation (not per message) to reduce traffic.
**Media:** compress/transcode on device, upload with background URLSession (resumable), show progress; thumbnails inline in the message for fast display.
**Push in background:** Notification Service Extension fetches/decrypts the message, writes it to the shared App Group DB so the app opens already up to date.
**Scale numbers:** 1B messages/day ≈ 12k/s average; group fan-out on server; clients only handle their own conversations.
**Edge cases:** message edited/deleted (tombstones), clock skew, app killed during send (outbox retried on launch), blocked users, very large groups (paginate members, no per-member receipts).
